newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila stocks end 1.56 pct up on window-dressing.
newsitem.headline: Manila stocks end 1.56 pct up on window-dressing.

text.p: Manila shares surged on Thursday to close 48.58 points, or 1.56 percent, up at 3,154.38 points as fund managers resorted to window-dressing and positioning for next year, said traders.
"With the U.S. interest rate issue out of the way, foreign fund managers are starting to come out," said Raul Ruiz, vice president at Sun Hung Kai Securities.
Value turnover was heavy at 3.7 billion pesos.

"The non-adjustment in U.S. interest rates also gave impetus to investors to start buying. Before the Fed's decision, people were hesitant to pick up stocks," said Jose Ma. Ricardo Garcia, executive vice-president at Diversified Securities Inc.
Gainers beat losers 75 to 42 with 65 issues unchanged. Traders said the rise in the index was supported largely by the property, commercial-industrial and banking sectors.
Positioning was seen in blue-chips such as Petron Corp, Ayala Corp and PCI Bank.
Garcia said that with the market gaining close to 50 points today, a slight pullback may be seen on Friday.
